forecasts.question: Will AGI be developed before 1 January 2030?
forecasts.key_change: Hold at 25%. May 1 2026: no new AGI declaration. Late-April backdrop unchanged—Anthropic still withholding Claude Mythos 5; Google announced up to $40B Anthropic investment (Apr 24) and unveiled new AI agents at Cloud Next; DeepMind's Hassabis reiterated AGI 'within five years' but with no specific milestone declaration. Frontier release cadence remains rapid but no credible lab has publicly claimed AGI. ~43 months to resolution; resolution criteria still hinge on a public declaration.
forecasts.base_rate: ~25% aggregated from Metaculus, Kalshi and expert surveys for AGI by 2029
factors_up: Continued rapid frontier release cadence (+2pp)
Hassabis publicly maintaining 'within five years' AGI timeline (+2pp)
Google's $40B Anthropic deal signals expectation of frontier AGI-class capability (+1pp)
Anthropic still withholding Mythos 5 as 'too capable' (+1pp)
factors_down: No credible lab has publicly claimed AGI achievement (-4pp)
AGI definition remains contested across labs and researchers (-3pp)
Resolution window narrowing to <44 months (-2pp)
Recent capability gains concentrated in narrow benchmarks (ARC-AGI-2), not broad agentic deployment (-1pp)
key_uncertainties: Whether withheld near-frontier models trigger a coordinated AGI declaration
Whether benchmark gains generalise to economically valuable agentic work
Whether 3+ leading researchers coordinate on a public AGI declaration

update_triggers.up: Major lab publicly declares AGI; 3+ leading researchers endorse a specific milestone; ARC-AGI-2 saturated
update_triggers.down: Stall in frontier capability gains; major labs walk back timelines; capex pullback

forecasts.question: Will economic consultancy lose ≥33% value/jobs by end 2030 due to AI?
forecasts.key_change: Hold at 20%. May 1 2026 update: McKinsey continues to absorb non-client role cuts (~5,000 roles since 2023); BCG, Bain, KPMG, Deloitte similarly trimming entry-level pyramids. Bloomberg (Apr 15) confirms ~25% of entry-level consulting/finance postings now require AI skills. Direction of travel consistent with priors but no abrupt jump in either revenue or employment metrics; ≥33% threshold still demanding given ~55 months to resolution.
forecasts.base_rate: Limited base rate; analogous tech disruptions (e.g., legal research, audit tooling) typically take 5–10 years to compress 30%+ of value
factors_up: McKinsey 5k+ role contraction since 2023 (+3pp)
WEF estimates ~100M white-collar jobs at risk over 5 years (+2pp)
Tier-1 firms publicly redesigning workforces around AI (+2pp)
Junior pyramid roles automating fastest, hitting consultancy structure directly (+1pp)
factors_down: Aggregate consultancy revenue still growing in 2025-26 (-4pp)
AI-augmented consulting may expand TAM rather than collapse it (-3pp)
33% is a high bar requiring rapid, broad-based decline (-2pp)
Procurement cycles in regulated sectors slow displacement (-2pp)
key_uncertainties: Whether 2027-2029 sees a step-change in client substitution of internal AI for external advisory
How '≥33% from 2024 baseline' will be measured and attributed by analysts
Whether one or two prestige firms tip into significant decline and pull aggregates down

update_triggers.up: Big-3 firm announces ≥15% revenue decline; major client publicly cancels strategy retainers citing AI
update_triggers.down: Sustained double-digit revenue growth at top 5 consultancies; explicit AI-augmented productivity uplift in earnings

forecasts.question: Will Labour be largest party at next UK General Election?
forecasts.key_change: Hold at 3%. May 1 2026: Electoral Calculus April MRP (23 Apr) shows Reform at 24% (down from 31% in January) but still projected as the largest party; combined Lab+Con vote share at 37.1% vs. 57.4% in 2024. Greens projected to take 74 seats with 68 from Labour, capping any Labour rebound. Labour remains in third place in headline polls. Election expected by end-2029.
forecasts.base_rate: UK incumbent parties at this stage of a parliament rarely recover to 'largest party' without major realignment; ~10-15% base for incumbent recovery from third place
factors_up: Reform vote share down 7pp since January (+2pp)
Possibility of Reform-Restore Britain split (+1pp)
Time horizon (~3.5 years) allows for major shocks (+1pp)
factors_down: Labour stuck in third place across MRP and headline polls (-4pp)
Green surge cannibalising 68+ Labour seats (-3pp)
Reform still leading projection despite vote share fall (-2pp)
No evident Starmer-government turnaround narrative (-2pp)
key_uncertainties: Whether Labour can reclaim Green-leaning seats with policy repositioning
Whether Reform fragments before the GE
Election timing—earlier elections favour incumbents less

update_triggers.up: Labour breaks 28%+ in 2+ polls; Reform-Restore Britain coalition collapses

forecasts.question: Will UK annual CPI inflation fall below 2.0% for at least one month before 1 January 2027?
forecasts.key_change: Hold at 1%. May 1 2026: ONS March 2026 CPI at 3.3% (released 22 Apr), up from 3.0% Feb. April 2026 CPI release scheduled 20 May 2026. Core CPI 3.1%, services 4.5%, goods 2.1%. factors_up: Energy base effects could drop sharply if oil retreats (+1pp)
Core services slowing in Q4 2026 if labour market loosens (+0pp)
factors_down: March 2026 print up to 3.3% from 3.0% (-2pp)
Services inflation 4.5%, sticky (-2pp)
Middle East energy upside risk (-1pp)

Whether services pay growth decelerates faster than expected
Possibility of fiscal price-cap measures distorting headline rate

update_triggers.up: Single-month CPI print drops below 2.5%; oil price collapses
update_triggers.down: Energy or food shock pushes CPI above 4%

forecasts.question: Will UK average annual real GDP growth exceed 1.5% across the 2030s (2030-2039)?
forecasts.key_change: Hold at 42%. May 1 2026: Most recent OBR EFO (March 2026) projects 1.6% average GDP growth across 2027-2030 with productivity rising as output gap closes. AI-driven productivity remains the principal upside swing factor; labour supply, fiscal drag, and energy transition costs the main downside. Long horizon means most variance unresolved.

factors_up: OBR projects 1.6% across 2027-2030 (+3pp)
Potential AI/productivity uplift in late-2020s spilling into 2030s (+3pp)
